A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same augmentation framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original supervised-learning, contrastive-pretraining, transfer, size-generalization, heuristic-accuracy, and computational-overhead experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds supervised-pretraining comparisons, temperature sensitivity, and QPLIB fitting results in Appendix E.3–E.5.

M1.justification: The KKT-based transformations, graph representation, MPNN architecture, supervised augmentation procedure, and NT-Xent pretraining remain unchanged. The added pretraining comparisons and expanded mathematical explanation do not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only generated LP/QP instances. v2 additionally uses five selected QPLIB instances after relaxing integer constraints, extending coverage to heterogeneous benchmark problems. This is a fitting experiment, not held-out benchmark generalization; the original dataset families remain.

E2.justification: Appendix E.3 and Table 8 add supervised pretraining with and without augmentation to the existing set-cover comparison between contrastive pretraining and training from scratch. The original augmentation and graph-SSL comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces a distinct protocol: pretraining on 10,000 random QPs with 1,000–1,500 variables and constraints, followed by 100-epoch fitting and evaluation on the same QPLIB instances. Supervised-pretraining controls and a temperature sweep are also added. Existing split-based experiments retain their settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.3 tests whether supervised pretraining, with or without augmentation, transfers to set cover. Appendix E.4 tests temperature values 0.01, 0.1, and 1 on LPs. Existing augmentation comparisons, heuristic analysis, overhead measurements, and size-generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new QPLIB experiment explicitly averages three random-seed runs and reports means without dispersion. The original five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged; this is not a reduction in runs for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New Tables 8–9 report supervised-pretraining and temperature results, including 1.034±0.055 for augmented supervised pretraining with 10% set-cover finetuning data. Table 11 adds QPLIB fitting outcomes: after 100 epochs, QPLIB_3694 predictions are 10.362 from scratch and 0.142 with pretraining, against an optimum of 0.000.

T1.justification: The derivation of Eq. (7) replaces the earlier automatic pseudo-inverse cancellation explanation with an explicit right-inverse identity and full-column-rank requirement on M. Associated rank discussion is revised. The propositions and appendix proofs otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: principled optimality-preserving augmentation, supervised and contrastive use, and improved generalization and transfer. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E.5 adds discussion of coefficient perturbations breaking feasibility or producing nearly identical training and test instances. It interprets QPLIB results as faster fitting and acknowledges that the advantage can diminish with longer training because evaluation uses training instances. Appendix E.3 also discusses the effectiveness of supervised pretraining.

D1.justification: The QPLIB experiment adds instance identifiers, dimensions and matrix densities, integer-relaxation instructions, and a reported pretraining cost of roughly 30 seconds per epoch on four NVIDIA L40S GPUs. Existing generation algorithms, augmentation hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2024b), An efficient unsupervised framework for convex quadratic programs via deep unrolling, and contrasts coefficient-perturbation evaluation with its QPLIB approach. Most apparent related-work expansion is existing material moved from v1 Appendix C into Section 1.1.

P1.justification: Related work is consolidated into Section 1.1, subsequent appendices are renumbered, the Eq. (7) explanation is expanded, and prose and headings receive local edits. The overall argument and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–11 for the new comparisons, sensitivity analysis, and QPLIB statistics/results. Figure 2 is resized and relocated, and existing tables and algorithms are repaginated. The original figures and established table designs are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The added pretraining controls and temperature analysis provide useful empirical support, while QPLIB results supply limited evidence about fitting larger benchmark instances. These are modest gains: QPLIB evaluation has no held-out test, and Appendix A still incorrectly describes evaluation as solely synthetic. The core method, claims, and original results remain unchanged.
